businesses.business: credit management and debt collection services

offering_description.value: Provides credit management services, mainly collecting overdue consumer and commercial receivables on behalf of banks, utilities, telecoms and other creditors, and purchasing and servicing portfolios of non-performing loans. Operates across Europe through a servicing platform and investor partnerships.

primary_products.value: purchased non-performing loan portfolios; debt portfolio investments

primary_services.value: debt collection; credit management; receivables servicing; portfolio servicing for investors; payment and pre-delinquency services

customer_segment.value: B2B: banks, financial institutions, utilities, telecoms, retailers and credit investors; B2C: indebted consumers who repay overdue balances through collection; B2G: public sector entities such as tax authorities and municipalities as creditors

end_markets.value: banking and financial services; telecommunications; utilities; retail; public sector

revenue_model.value: commissions or management fees: fees and commissions on collections for creditors and investor portfolio servicing; other: returns from collections on owned purchased non-performing loan portfolios

value_chain_position.value: service provider: collects receivables for creditor clients and services investor-owned portfolios; financial intermediary: buys non-performing loans from banks and recovers cash from debtors, with co-investors

geography_served.value: global: Mainly Europe, with operations in about 20 European markets, led by the Nordics, Germany, Spain, Italy and the UK

specialization.value: related lines: collection services and non-performing loan investing and servicing

distribution_channels.value: direct sales: relationships with banks, utilities, telecoms and investors, including portfolio sale tenders; online: digital payment and self-service portals for debtors

regulatory_exposure.value: high: debt collection licensing and consumer protection, plus data privacy (GDPR), under national regulators and EU rules

notes: Intrum restructured in 2024-25 (Chapter 11 plan, new capital structure) and has been shifting toward a servicing-focused, capital-light model; exact current market list and mix of investing versus servicing are uncertain.
